program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s repeated, high-confidence “complete” judgments conflict with the aggregate reference “partial,” but the traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure. The edited image does show substantial chalk-like rendering—grainy, softened outlines and smudged shading—while retaining the giraffes and scene; the reference label alone does not establish which visual feature makes the transformation incomplete. Improve the criterion/binding so it distinguishes a fully chalk-drawn image from partial stylization using observable evidence across the whole image, rather than treating any chalk-like texture as sufficient or inferring incompleteness from preserved content. In particular, assess whether photographic detail or other non-chalk rendering remains in significant regions, and require evidence for that distinction before assigning partial versus complete. Keep unknown available when the image does not support a reliable distinction; do not lower confidence or change the label merely to match the reference. The stable repeated judgments are a reason to investigate this criterion boundary, not evidence that the requested edit is absent.
